class.name: NetwCompTable
class.brief_description: The one-byte component address for one entity: what a comp id names.
class.description: Ids are positions in the sorted path list, so two peers that registered the same sub-nodes in different orders still agree on every id. Registration order is a property of whichever code happened to run, and the wire cannot carry it, so an id keyed on it disagrees between peers for a reason neither peer can see. The table refuses rather than guesses, and its three refusals are different facts. A hash the authority did not author leaves it [member poisoned], because the two structures disagree and every id is then a coin flip. An id outside the mapping names nothing. A fallback path that could leave the entity subtree is refused on its shape, before anything resolves it, because resolution is the work a hostile address wants done. [codeblock] comp 0 the entity root comp 1..254 the table's path for that id, or nothing comp 255 `path`, once proven to land inside the entity subtree [/codeblock] [method classify] answers without looking at the tree and so can only leave the descendant proof owed; [method resolve_node] is that question with the proof discharged, and is what a caller holding the entity root asks.

method.name: assign
method.description: Adopts [param paths] as the whole table, sorted, ids assigned by position. Paths past the addressable range keep their place in the order and gain no id, so a digest built over [method sorted_paths] covers the structure rather than the addressable part of it.

method.name: classify
method.description: Returns what the address [param comp] and [param path] names, as one of [enum Address], before any node is resolved. A [constant ADDRESS_RELATIVE] answer still owes a proof that what it resolves to is a descendant of the entity root, which only the resolved node can give, so a caller that means to reach the node asks [method resolve_node] instead.

method.name: resolve_node
method.description: Returns the node [param comp] and [param path] address under [param owner], or [code]null[/code]. [constant ADDRESS_ROOT] answers [param owner], [constant ADDRESS_MAPPED] the node at this table's path for [param comp], and [constant ADDRESS_RELATIVE] the node at [param path] once it is [param owner] or a descendant of it. Every other [enum Address], and a [param path] naming nothing, answers [code]null[/code]. An [param owner] that is not a live [Node] addresses nothing, which is the answer for an entity with no node rather than a check each caller keeps. An address arrives off the wire and chooses its own [param comp], so the descendant proof lives here: a caller that only classified is a caller that can still be handed a node outside the subtree.

method.name: has_path
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] when [param path] carries an id here.

method.name: id_for_path
method.description: Returns the id registered for [param path], or [code]0[/code] when it has none. Ids start at [code]1[/code], so guard with [method has_path] where [code]0[/code] has to be told apart from a miss.

method.name: path_for_id
method.description: Returns the path registered under [param id], empty when no path carries it.

method.name: path_shape_is_safe
method.description: Rejects a [param path] that is absolute, parent-relative, or a resource path. A shape-safe relative path can only reach descendants of the root it is resolved against, which is why containment is a separate question the caller answers with the node it got back rather than with the string.

method.name: reconcile
method.description: Settles [member table_hash] against [member wire_hash] and returns whether the call poisoned the table. Authority authors the digest; anyone else compares against it.

method.name: sorted_paths
method.description: Returns the table in id order, which is the order a digest reads it in.

members.member: [code]true[/code] once this peer's structure disagreed with the authority's, so every id answers [constant ADDRESS_UNMAPPED] and routed frames fall back to paths instead of misrouting.
This peer's own digest of its structure. The digest is composed by the caller, because what it covers reaches past this table into the scripts an id addresses.
The digest the authority authored, carried on the spawn packet.

constants.constant: The entity root itself, which every entity has.
The table's path for this id, trusted because the table is local.
The frame's own path, still owed a descendant proof by the caller.
A shape that can leave the subtree. Never resolved.
No path carries this id here.
